hebrews.7.p1.b1.text: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High.

hebrews.7.p1.b2.text: He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

hebrews.7.p1.b3.text: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything.

hebrews.7.p1.b4.text: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.

hebrews.7.p2.b5.text: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.

hebrews.7.p2.b6.text: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people …

hebrews.7.p2.b7.text: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

hebrews.7.p2.b8.text: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor.

hebrews.7.p3.b9.text: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood (for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear …

hebrews.7.p3.b10.text: … one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?

hebrews.7.p3.b11.text: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.

hebrews.7.p3.b12.text: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priests.

hebrews.7.p4.b13.text: one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power of an indestructible life.

hebrews.7.p4.b14.text: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

hebrews.7.p4.b15.text: So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless (for the law made nothing perfect),

hebrews.7.p4.b16.text: and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God.

hebrews.7.p5.b17.text: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’”

hebrews.7.p5.b18.text: Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.

hebrews.7.p5.b19.text: But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.

hebrews.7.p5.b20.text: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.

hebrews.7.p6.b21.text: Such a high priest truly befits us—One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.

hebrews.7.p6.b22.text: Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people;

hebrews.7.p6.b23.text: He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.

hebrews.7.p6.b24.text: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
